entities.summary: ISIS, short for Intel System Implementation Supervisor, was an operating system for early Intel microprocessors like the 8080. It was originally developed by Ken Burgett and Jim Stein under the management of Steve Hanna and Terry Opdendyk for the Intel Microprocessor Development System with two 8" floppy drives, starting in 1975, and later adopted as ISIS-II as the operating system for the PL/M compiler, assembler, link editor, and In-Circuit Emulator. The ISIS operating system was developed on an early prototype of the MDS 800 computer, the same type of hardware that Gary Kildall used to develop CP/M.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The ISIS operating system played a crucial role in the development of early Intel microprocessors and influenced the creation of CP/M, an influential personal computer operating system. Its impact was significant for the burgeoning personal computing industry in the late 1970s.
